name: Magmatic (orthomagmatic)
description: Crystals settle into cumulate layers within a magma chamber.

name: Magmatic-hydrothermal
description: A cooling intrusion feeds branching veins within an alteration halo.

name: Metamorphic / orogenic hydrothermal
description: Compression folds the host rocks; a shear-controlled quartz vein cuts the sequence.

name: Basinal and diagenetic hydrothermal
description: Brines move through a sedimentary basin toward a fault and stratabound trap.

name: Submarine hydrothermal (seawater-convection driven)
description: Seawater descends beside black smokers above a submarine heat source.

name: Sedimentary and chemical-sedimentary
description: Particles precipitate and settle through water into mineral-rich beds.

name: Surficial and weathering
description: Percolating water produces a weathering profile and irregular reaction front.

name: Clastic / mechanical (placer and palaeoplacer)
description: Flowing water sorts gravel and concentrates dense grains at a channel base.

name: Hybrid, industrial and other systems
description: A mineral-bearing specimen combines clay sheets, a prism and a faceted gemstone.

name: Magmatic sulfide (Ni-Cu-PGE)
description: A feeder enters a mafic intrusion; immiscible sulfide droplets collect at its base.

name: Magmatic oxide (Cr, Fe-Ti-V)
description: Dense oxide layers accumulate within a mafic magma chamber.

name: Carbonatite and alkaline-igneous
description: A concentric alkaline-carbonatite ring complex with radial dykes.

name: Granitic pegmatite
description: A coarse-crystalline dyke with large interlocking prisms and a mica book.

name: Kimberlite and lamproite
description: A crater-topped, tapering volcanic pipe carries a deep diamond.

name: Porphyry
description: Stockwork veinlets and nested alteration zones surround an intrusive cupola.

name: Skarn and carbonate-replacement
description: A garnet-bearing reaction zone separates an intrusion from carbonate beds.

name: Epithermal
description: A shallow banded vein rises beneath a volcanic surface and sinter terrace.

name: Other intrusion-related
description: Sheeted veins extend above a granitic cupola.

name: Iron oxide-alkali-altered
description: Angular breccia fragments sit in an iron-oxide-rich matrix with mineralized pathways.

name: Orogenic gold
description: A quartz-gold shear vein crosses folded host rocks.

name: Sediment-hosted disseminated gold
description: Fine gold is disseminated through a reactive sedimentary layer above a dark bed.

name: Metamorphic industrial minerals
description: Graphite and pale mineral sheets form books within a folded host.

name: Sediment-hosted Zn-Pb
description: A fault feeds bedded sulfides with contrasting sulfide crystal habits.

name: Sediment-hosted stratiform Cu
description: A thin mineralized horizon follows the boundary beneath red beds.

name: Basinal and groundwater uranium
description: Groundwater flows toward a crescent-shaped roll front in a sandstone aquifer.

name: Basinal and polymetallic vein
description: A branching mineral vein contains a fluorite form and a barite blade.

name: Volcanogenic massive sulfide
description: A massive sulfide lens overlies a stringer zone beneath a seafloor chimney.

name: Chemical sediment Fe-Mn
description: Iron-rich and pale bands are paired with a concentric manganese nodule.

name: Chemical and biochemical sediment (P, evaporite, black shale)
description: Chemical precipitates and evaporite crystals accumulate above stratified sediment.

name: Residual and lateritic
description: A nodular ferric cap overlies a mottled, mineral-enriched weathering profile.

name: Supergene sulfide and non-sulfide
description: Downward leaching forms a secondary enrichment blanket beneath an oxidized cap.

name: Evaporative and brine
description: Evaporation above a closed basin concentrates brine and salt beneath its surface.

name: Placer and palaeoplacer
description: A meandering river concentrates dense grains on the inside of bends.

name: Industrial minerals and rocks
description: Clay sheets, quartz prisms and a carbonate block represent industrial feedstocks.

name: Gemstone systems
description: A large faceted gem and contrasting natural crystal prisms.

name: Energy-adjacent and excluded systems
description: A dark coal seam and geothermal well represent the corpus cross-reference category.

name: Komatiite-hosted Ni-Cu-(PGE)
description: A komatiite flow with spinifex blades banks over a footwall embayment holding a massive sulfide pool.

name: Conduit- and intrusion-hosted Ni-Cu-(PGE)
description: A magma conduit cuts the host sediments and drops sulfide at a dilation along its path.

name: Layered-intrusion PGE reef and contact deposits
description: A single sulfide reef runs through the cumulate layers of a layered intrusion.

name: Stratiform (layered-intrusion) chromitite
description: Stacked chromitite seams repeat through a layered mafic intrusion.

name: Podiform (ophiolitic) chromite
description: Chromite pods lie in the foliated mantle rocks of an ophiolite.

name: Fe-Ti-(V-P) oxide in mafic intrusions
description: A discordant oxide lens with apatite crystals cuts the layering of a mafic intrusion.

name: Alaskan-Ural type zoned ultramafic Pt
description: Concentric ultramafic zones ring the platinum-bearing dunite core of a vertical pipe.

name: Carbonatite-associated REE-Nb-P
description: A carbonatite plug with ring dykes carries rare earths inside a fenite halo.

name: Alkaline-peralkaline REE-Zr-Nb-(Y-Be-Li)
description: Inclined layers of an alkaline complex carry rare earth, zirconium and niobium minerals.

name: LCT (Li-Cs-Ta) pegmatite
description: A zoned pegmatite dyke in foliated host rock carries spodumene laths and lepidolite books.

name: NYF (Nb-Y-F) pegmatite
description: Crystals line a miarolitic cavity inside a granite-hosted pegmatite with graphic texture.

name: Kimberlite- and lamproite-hosted diamond
description: A tuff ring, crater, diatreme and root zone make up a diamond-bearing kimberlite pipe.

name: Porphyry Cu-(Au-Mo)
description: Nested alteration shells and a veinlet stockwork surround a copper-bearing porphyry cupola.

name: Alkalic porphyry Cu-Au
description: A narrow alkalic porphyry pipe carries gold with carbonate veins and magnetite.

name: Porphyry Mo
description: An inverted-cup molybdenite ore shell arches over a small high-silica stock.

name: Porphyry W and porphyry Sn
description: Sheeted quartz veins above a cupola carry wolframite blades and cassiterite.

name: Skarn (metal-classified)
description: Zoned garnet and pyroxene bands follow the contact between an intrusion and limestone.

name: Carbonate-replacement / Cordilleran polymetallic (Zn-Pb-Ag-Cu)
description: A sulfide chimney feeds flat replacement mantos out through the limestone beds.

name: Volcanic-hosted strata-bound (manto) Cu
description: A strata-bound copper layer follows a permeable flow top in amygdaloidal volcanics.

name: High-sulfidation epithermal Au-Ag-(Cu)
description: Vuggy residual silica sits inside the advanced argillic lithocap of a volcanic edifice.

name: Intermediate-sulfidation epithermal Ag-Au-Zn-Pb
description: A banded carbonate-base metal vein carries sphalerite and galena.

name: Low-sulfidation epithermal Au-Ag
description: A colloform-banded vein with bladed calcite rises to a sinter terrace at the surface.

name: Reduced intrusion-related gold system
description: Sheeted gold-bearing quartz veins fill the apex of a reduced granite cupola.

name: Granite-related Sn-W (greisen, vein, breccia)
description: A greisen cap and quartz lodes above a granite carry cassiterite.

name: Be-F-(Li-U) volcanic replacement
description: A fluorite-rich replacement layer follows a tuff bed beneath a rhyolite dome.

name: Intrusive, metasomatite and volcanic-hosted uranium
description: Pale alaskite sheets cut foliated gneiss and carry uranium oxide.

name: Iron oxide copper-gold (IOCG)
description: A hematite breccia pipe with rotated clasts carries copper and gold.

name: Iron oxide-apatite (IOA / Kiruna type)
description: A massive magnetite body with apatite crystals sits in volcanic host rocks.

name: Orogenic (mesothermal) gold
description: A laminated quartz lode follows a shear zone, with tension gashes in the walls.

name: Listwaenite / ultramafic-hosted carbonate-replacement gold
description: Carbonate alteration replaces serpentinite along a fault, with gold in quartz gashes.

name: Epizonal Sb-Hg (and Sb-Au)
description: Radiating stibnite blades fill a shallow quartz vein close to the surface.

name: Carlin-type sediment-hosted disseminated gold
description: Jasperoid replaces a receptive carbonate bed above a steep feeder fault.

name: Metamorphic and vein graphite
description: Graphite seams follow the folds, with flake books and a crosscutting vein.

name: Magnesite, talc and related ultramafic-hosted industrial minerals
description: A magnesite stockwork cuts an ultramafic body with talc along its upper contact.

name: Clastic-dominated (SEDEX) Zn-Pb-Ag
description: A laminated sulfide lens thins away from a syn-sedimentary feeder fault.

name: Mississippi Valley-type Zn-Pb
description: Collapse breccia in a karst void carries sphalerite and galena from migrating brines.

name: Irish-type carbonate-hosted Zn-Pb
description: Sulfide builds at the base of a carbonate wedge against a syn-rift normal fault.

name: Sediment-hosted stratiform (and red-bed) Cu-Co
description: Zoned copper and sulfide bands follow a redox front between red beds and grey shale.

name: Unconformity-related uranium
description: An ore lens straddles the unconformity where a graphitic fault meets the sandstone.

name: Sandstone-hosted uranium
description: A crescent roll front separates oxidised from reduced sand in a channel.

name: Five-element (Ag-Ni-Co-As-Bi) vein
description: Cockade bands and silver dendrites fill a carbonate vein.

name: Fluorite-barite vein and strata-bound deposits
description: A fluorite vein feeds strata-bound flats, with barite blades at the top.

name: Volcanogenic massive sulfide (VMS)
description: A massive sulfide mound caps a discordant stringer zone in altered volcanics.

name: Modern seafloor massive sulfide (SMS)
description: Active chimneys and plumes stand in a rift valley on the modern seafloor.

name: Iron formation (BIF and GIF)
description: Rhythmic iron and chert bands repeat through a tilted iron formation.

name: Sedimentary and volcano-sedimentary manganese
description: A manganese oxide bed of ooids settles on a shallow shelf.

name: Deep-sea ferromanganese nodules and crusts
description: Nodules litter the abyssal floor beside a manganese crust on a seamount flank.

name: Phosphorite
description: Upwelling feeds a pelletal phosphate bed at the shelf edge.

name: Black shale-hosted polymetallic (Ni-Mo-Zn-V-U-PGE)
description: Pyrite laminae and a polymetallic layer sit within anoxic black shale.

name: Evaporite potash, salt and polyhalite
description: Cyclic halite, anhydrite and potash beds form beneath an evaporating brine.

name: Bauxite (lateritic and karst)
description: A pisolitic bauxite layer caps the clay and bedrock of a weathering profile.

name: Nickel (-cobalt-scandium) laterite
description: Garnierite veins cut the saprolite between limonite cover and serpentinite bedrock.

name: Ion-adsorption clay REE
description: Rare earths adsorb onto clay platelets in regolith above weathered granite.

name: Supergene-enriched iron ore
description: Leaching upgrades banded iron formation to high-grade hematite beneath a hardcap.

name: Channel iron deposit (pisolitic palaeochannel iron)
description: Pisolitic iron ore fills an incised palaeochannel.

name: Supergene copper (leached cap, oxide and chalcocite enrichment)
description: A leached cap, oxide zone and chalcocite blanket stack above the water table.

name: Non-sulfide (supergene) zinc
description: Oxide zinc ore fills a karst cavity above a relict sulfide body.

name: Continental, geothermal and oilfield lithium brine
description: Brine sits beneath the halite crust of a closed salar.

name: Sedimentary and volcano-sedimentary lithium clay
description: Lithium-bearing clay beds fill a volcanic basin.

name: Borate and nitrate (arid-basin non-halide evaporite)
description: Borate crystal beds grow beneath the cracked crust of an arid playa.

name: Surficial (calcrete) uranium
description: Carnotite sits in valley calcrete above the water table.

name: Placer and palaeoplacer gold
description: Gold collects in bedrock riffles beneath a gravel terrace.

name: Quartz-pebble conglomerate (Witwatersrand-type) Au-U
description: Rounded quartz pebbles and gold line a tilted conglomerate reef.

name: Heavy mineral sands (Ti-Zr-REE)
description: Dark heavy-mineral laminae follow the beach face and dune.

name: Placer tin (and associated Nb-Ta)
description: Cassiterite-bearing gravel fills a drowned bedrock valley beneath marine mud.

name: Placer and marine-placer diamond
description: Diamonds settle into bedrock potholes beneath river gravel.

name: Industrial minerals (kaolin, bentonite, zeolite, silica, gypsum, limestone, diatomite)
description: Quarry benches step down through industrial mineral beds to a product stockpile.

name: Gemstone deposits (emerald, corundum, opal, jade, garnet)
description: A beryl prism grows in a vein cutting schist, beside corundum and an opal nodule.

name: Coal, oil shale, hydrocarbon and geothermal systems
description: A coal seam, an anticlinal hydrocarbon trap and rising geothermal heat share one section.
